extracted.intended_audience: researchers, university administrators, hiring committees, research assessment professionals, and grant/faculty recruitment policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and quality-control of external peer review and bibliometric assessment used in recruiting Assistant Professors and Senior Researchers; includes construction of a composite bibliometric score and statistical tests for gender bias in reviewer merit scores. Focus is on empirical analysis of a university career-ladder recruitment process and recommendations to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite bibliometric score
rubrics_metrics.description: A composite score adapted from previous work, consisting of seven standardized bibliometric variables (sum yields range 0–7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from seven parts: (1) number of publications, (2) total citations, (3) share of first-author publications, (4) share of last-author publications, (5) H index, (6) share of publications in high impact journals within its field, and (7) binary indicator for any publication in a high impact journal overall. Each part is log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool so that the smallest value = 0 and the largest = 1; the composite score is the sum of the seven standardized variables (possible range 0 to 7). Guidance notes: the score is calculated on publications/reviews from 1995 to application date in Web of Science and should be verified manually via PMIDs and author position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of publications (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of publications (articles and reviews) published from 1995 to application time and recorded in Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications were manually verified by librarians using PMID, journal, title, and author to ensure correct matching and author position; part of the composite bibliometric score and log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total number of citations (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of citations to the applicant's included publications as retrieved from Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an impact indicator in the composite score; log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool. Note: citation metrics can be gender-biased and may require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of publications as first author (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion (share) of the applicant's publications where they are listed as first author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted as ability to lead a project at a junior level; included in composite score, log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of publications as last author (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion (share) of the applicant's publications where they are listed as last (senior) author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted as ability to lead a project at a senior level; included in composite score, log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: H index (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's H index calculated from the included publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents consistency of impact across publications; included in composite score, log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of publications in high-impact journals within field (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of the applicant's papers published in journals considered high impact within their Clarivate-defined field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field defined using Clarivate journal categorization; within-field high-impact journals = top two journals by Journal Impact Factor; this variable is included in the composite score, log-transformed and normalized within the applicant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary indicator for any publication in a high-impact journal (composite component)
rubrics_metrics.description: A binary (yes/no) indicator for whether the applicant has any publication in a high-impact journal overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall high-impact journals defined as the top 30 journals by Journal Impact Factor; included in composite score as a binary 'bonus' and normalized as part of the seven components.

rubrics_metrics.name: External reviewer merit score (0–7 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: External non-KI reviewers provide one score for merits based on CV and publications and one for the project plan; merit scores range 0–7 with anchored descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale anchoring used by KI: 7 = Exceptional, 6 = Excellent, 5 = Very good to Excellent, 4 = Very Good, 3 = Good, 2 = Weak, 1 = Poor, 0 = Insufficient information provided for assessment. Six external reviewers (professors at other Swedish universities, equal gender distribution) scored each application and returned rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit score components (what reviewers assess)
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit scores are based on (1) publications and (2) academic education and research merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic education and research merits include education, experience of research, competence, independence, research network, financing, prizes, and invitations to present or review. Publications include published papers and scientific presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer score normalization and assessor-scale checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to detect and, if necessary, correct for differences in grading scales between assessors using Z-normalization and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Z-normalization: Z = (X – M)/S where X is an individual grade, M the assessor mean, and S the assessor standard deviation; ICCs computed before/after standardization to test homogeneity. In this dataset ICCs were sufficiently high in 2014–2016 so normalization was not deemed necessary from 2017 onward. Analyses in the paper were performed on non-normalized data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment process procedural thresholds (three-step Career Ladder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-step process used by KI Career Ladder: Step 1 selection of top 30% of applicants for external review; Step 2 external review by six reviewers scoring merits and project plan; Step 3 interviews of top ~20 applicants for final selection to positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No selection based on research field or type of research. Typical final positions: 7–11 Assistant Professor positions or 6–8 Senior Researcher positions. Applicant pooling and selection rules (e.g., top 30% cutoff) are part of the procedural rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite score calculation constraints and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications included were those available in Web of Science from 1995 to application date and were manually verified by KI librarians to ensure correct author matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PMIDs were incorrect, librarians matched by journal/title/author; if PMID matched but author missing, full text was checked. The composite score standardization was performed only on applicants selected for external review (selected applicants pool). When pooling years, repeat applicants were identified and only first application included for pooled analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-normalization and definition of high-impact journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Field was defined using Clarivate's journal categorization; within a field the top two journals by Journal Impact Factor were considered high impact; overall, the top 30 journals were considered high impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute the 6th and 7th components of the composite bibliometric score. Note caveat in paper: field- and citation-based metrics can themselves be biased and may need correction (e.g., field-specific 'bias factor').

rubrics_metrics.name: MeSH-term based field-segregation analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing gender segregation of research fields via applicant publication MeSH major descriptors and network analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants were linked to a MeSH term if at least two of their articles had the same MeSH term. To display anonymized nodes, at least two Assistant Professor applicants or three Senior Researcher applicants had to share the same MeSH term. Parental MeSH categories of the top 50 MeSH terms were retrieved to assess overlap; Venn diagrams and network figures were created to evaluate field overlap vs segregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and significance criteria for bias detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use linear regression models to quantify association between composite bibliometric score (x-variable) and external reviewer merit score (y-variable), including gender as a covariate and interaction term to test slope differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report slope estimate, gender effect, interaction term, R, R-square, degrees of freedom, F-statistic. P-values considered significant at p < 0.05. Analyses in R (version 3.6.0). Stratify analyses by gender and year when appropriate; remove repeat applicants for pooled analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition and reviewer number considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical practice in the studied calls: six external reviewers per application, with equal gender distribution; literature suggests reliability improves with more reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KI used six reviewers (professors at other Swedish universities). The paper cites Forscher et al. (2019) suggesting at least 12 reviewers may be needed for reliable evaluations of NIH R01 applications; granting bodies should consider reviewer number for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-step semi-blinded review recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed process to minimize bias: (1) blinded review of project plans (when applicants are junior), (2) compute composite bibliometric score as objective measure of past productivity, (3) individual reviewer integrates project-plan score and composite bibliometric score into an overall assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note bibliometry is itself biased (citation bias) and suggest corrections (e.g., field-specific bias factor). They recommend piloting via field experiments and stress the need for further research to confirm that this procedure better identifies top-qualified individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality-control self-assessment for granting bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting bodies should self-assess peer-review procedures by testing whether merit/competence scores correlate with applicant productivity and whether scoring is matched for men and women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested actions include computing correlations between reviewer scores and objective productivity metrics and testing for gender differences in these correlations; adapt processes if discrepancies indicate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training and instructions about bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions given to reviewers in the studied calls contained no instructions concerning gender bias or suggestions for how to handle bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend that institutions implement awareness efforts and provide web training programs for reviewers; reviewer instructions should explicitly address bias mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization and data-protection constraints for analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to privacy considerations, data are presented on a group level only to preclude identification of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses requiring field adjustment (e.g., regression controlling for subfield) may be limited by anonymization; thresholds for displaying MeSH nodes were applied to protect identity.
